Water boils at **100°C** (212°F) at sea level, which is defined as standard atmospheric pressure of 1 atmosphere (about 101.325 kPa or 14.7 psi).

This is actually how the Celsius scale was originally defined — 0°C was set as the freezing point of water and 100°C as the boiling point of water at sea level, with 100 equal divisions between them.
